payload.rationale: The forecast date is September 19, 2026, exactly three months before the scheduled December 18, 2026 release of Dune: Part Three. The official movie site is actively advertising this release date, along with international releases and specific early-access screenings on December 14 and 15. When a major tentpole film is within three months of release and advertising specific early-access dates, the likelihood of a delay is very low, as marketing budgets are already being heavily deployed and theatrical distribution agreements are locked. The strongest reason this estimate could be too high is that three months is typically past the point of no return for major delays, barring extraordinary circumstances like a sudden global crisis, making the true probability even closer to zero. The strongest reason this estimate could be too low is that complex VFX-heavy films occasionally suffer last-minute post-production bottlenecks, and the provided evidence notes some placeholder text on the site, which could hint at slightly lagging marketing assets or incomplete readiness.
limitations: An advertised schedule is not proof of completed post-production or a guarantee against delay.
Some character sections contain placeholder text, which could indicate incomplete marketing materials.
No historical delay base rate was fitted for films within 3 months of release.
